title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This page belongs to the part of the Teichmüller-groupoid notes where Grothendieck builds a formalism of 'Π-groupoids'. A Π-groupoid is a connected groupoid whose vertex groups are identified with a fixed group Π, compatibly with conjugation.

The previous page establishes equivalence (17). On one side are connected Π-groupoids Φ with an action of a group μ on (Φ, Π) such that Ob Φ is a μ-torsor. On the other side are extensions 1→Π→E→μ→1. Given Φ, one takes as E the set of pairs (g ∈ μ, arrow x → g·x), which is essentially the orbit-groupoid / quotient-stack fundamental group. Conversely E gives back Φ = 𝓔(E).

He then defines an 'E(Π,μ)-structure' on a groupoid C' over C. Over each object he wants an identification between the extension E_{C'} (attached to a point or component) and the fixed extension E. On this page he adds that one must specify how such isomorphisms pass from one to another for ξ1, ξ2 ∈ Ob C in the same connected component of C. This is a descent or coherence condition.

The model example used to make this precise:
- P is a U-torsor over T, with U a connected topological, Lie or algebraic group.
- Π = π1(U,1).
- μ ⊂ U is a discrete normal subgroup (18); it is automatically central.
- There are compatible maps E → P and μ → U.
- Passing to quotients gives the commutative square E → P, E_0 = E/μ → P_0 = P/μ, where q : P → P_0.
- P_0 is a U_0-torsor over T, with U_0 = U/μ (19).
- Since μ is discrete, the universal covers agree: Ũ_0 = Ũ. Hence π1(U_0,1) is an extension of μ by π1(U) = Π, and (20) identifies the extension E canonically with π1(U_0, 1_{U_0}).

The page breaks off ('π1(P_0) est muni d'un ...'); the next page completes it as an 'E-structure' (21): E → Aut(id_{Π1(P_0)}). Loops in the structure group U_0 act on the fundamental groupoid of the U_0-torsor P_0 through the action map U_0 × P_0 → P_0. This gives central natural automorphisms of the identity functor, i.e. π1 of the structure group maps to the centre of the fundamental groupoid of the torsor.

The aim is to show that the pullback groupoid C_0 (inverse image of Π1(P_0) along E_0 → P_0) can be rebuilt purely algebraically from C' with its Π-groupoid structure and μ-action. In other words, he wants a combinatorial description of passing to a quotient by a finite central subgroup of the structure group.

In the Teichmüller context the likely model is a C*-torsor such as the frame bundle of a determinant/Hodge line bundle (Π = Z) and μ = μ_n. Then π1(C*/μ_n) = Z, viewed as the extension 0→Z→Z→Z/n→0. This would govern central Z-extensions of Teichmüller groupoids and their n-th-root (level / spin-type) variants. This reading is plausible but not explicit on the page.
errors: Formula (20) as transcribed, 'E/Π ≃ π1(U_0,1_{U_0})', is inconsistent: E/Π ≅ μ. The mathematically correct statement, and almost certainly what is meant (the Π under E is likely an index or decoration), is E ≃ π1(U_0,1_{U_0}) as extensions of μ by Π = π1(U,1).

Tacit hypotheses: U is connected and μ is discrete, so that Ũ_0 = Ũ. Normality of μ then forces μ to be central. Since π1 of a topological group is abelian, the resulting extension E is abelian and in particular central. These are not stated on the page.
The coherence condition for changing isomorphisms between ξ1 and ξ2 in the same component is announced ('je présume') but not formulated on this page.

ideas.what: Equivalence between connected Π-groupoids with a μ-action that is free and transitive on objects, and extensions of μ by Π (recalled from the previous page as (17)).
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental group of a quotient / orbit groupoid; π1 of the quotient stack [X/G] as an extension of G by π1(X); groupoid-with-action ↔ group extension
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; R. Brown and P. Higgins / Taylor (orbit groupoids, 1970s–80s); SGA1-style exact sequences
ideas.where_published: Related exact sequences for Galois quotients appear in SGA1; this exact groupoid formulation is not known to me in his published texts

ideas.what: For a U-torsor P and a discrete central μ ⊂ U, the quotient P/μ is a U/μ-torsor, Ũ/μ-covers agree, and π1(U/μ) is an extension of μ by π1(U).
ideas.modern_name: Covering theory of topological groups; isogenies of structure groups

ideas.what: π1 of the structure group acts centrally on the fundamental groupoid of a torsor, giving a homomorphism π1(U_0) → Aut(id_{Π1(P_0)}).
ideas.modern_name: Centre of the fundamental groupoid; action of π1(G) on π1 of a principal G-bundle; banded gerbe / central structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (fibration exact sequences); the gerbe-band viewpoint goes to Giraud 1971

ideas.what: The notion of an 'E(Π,μ)-structure' on a groupoid over C, i.e. a coherent family of identifications of local extensions with a fixed extension, intended for describing quotients of Teichmüller groupoids by central finite subgroups.
ideas.modern_name: Torsor/gerbe-type rigidification; central extensions of mapping class groupoids
ideas.usually_credited_to: Central extensions of mapping class groups: Meyer, Atiyah, Witten-era TQFT literature (late 1980s)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets out to give a purely combinatorial ('purement algébrique') reconstruction of the groupoid C_0 obtained after dividing the structure group by a finite central μ. The input would be the Π-groupoid C' with μ-action. Applied to Teichmüller groupoids, this would be a discrete-groupoid description of central extensions and their μ-quotients (e.g. Z-extensions from line bundles and n-th-root variants). The thread breaks off before the coherence condition is formulated.
missed.quote: avec une condition de passage d'un tel isomorphisme à un autre je présume, pour ξ1, ξ2 ∈ C dans une même composante connexe de C
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Central extensions of mapping class groupoids (framings, determinant line bundles, spin/level structures) are central in TQFT and in Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory. A Teichmüller-groupoid-level formalism for them would be of mild interest historically, though the underlying mathematics is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine technical step: covering theory of a torsor quotiented by a discrete central subgroup, and the identification E ≃ π1(U/μ). It sits inside a non-standard groupoid formalism. The only mildly notable aspect is the implied programme of handling central extensions of Teichmüller groupoids combinatorially, which is not explicit here.
transcription_corrections: (20) should most likely read 𝓔 ≃ π1(U_0, 1_{U_0}); the 'Π' under 𝓔 is a decoration or index, not a quotient (E/Π would be μ).
First line: the extension seems to carry an index like 𝓔_{C'_ξ} or 𝓔_{C'}, i.e. the extension attached to the point ξ.
'pour ξ1, ξ2 ∈ C' is probably 'ξ1, ξ2 ∈ Ob C'.
Marginal note (middle left): 'On suppose μ ⊂ U (18), et μ distingué dans U' — this is the hypothesis label (18).
Top-left marginal note: 'C : NB pour récupérer C à partir de C', ... prendre ... 𝓔 = C'/𝓔(Π,μ)' — a reminder that C is recovered as a quotient of C'.
